title: Chapter 248: A Game That Can't be Cleared
html:
During lunch, Director Luo came to see Chen Ge in person. The packed rest tent pleased him. “Drawing this many visitors even at lunchtime is no small accomplishment.”

Director Luo sighed. Several weeks ago, the Haunted House had been the most deserted place at the park, but now it was the park’s main feature and saving grace.

“Director Luo? What brings you here?” Chen Ge held the boxed meal Xu Wan had bought in one hand while using the other to update his accounts.

“I have two pieces of good news.” Director Luo surveyed the makeshift tents, then handed Chen Ge the document he carried.

“It’s been a long time since I heard any.” Chen Ge opened the file. It contained his proposal for a visitor lounge, but his amateur sketch had been supplemented by detailed blueprints filled with annotations and explanations.

“This is?”

“The park may not be what it once was, but we can still provide this much financial support.” Director Luo appeared to be in an excellent mood. “Review the revised proposal. If anything needs changing, come see me.”

Chen Ge set aside his work and examined the plans carefully. He was extremely satisfied; they were far more detailed and considered than his original draft.

“Director Luo, what is the other good news?” Chen Ge raised his head. He was intrigued.

“Beginning tomorrow, park admission will fall to sixty yuan. We’ll also introduce promotions and discounts for group purchases.” Director Luo had finally made his decision. The futuristic park placed him under enormous pressure. Lowering prices was both a marketing strategy and a reluctant retreat.

“Lowering so much?” Ever since it opened its door, New Century Park’s ticket price had been rising; this was the first time it would fall.

“Lowering it voluntarily now is better than being forced to later.” Director Luo accepted the decision pragmatically. “If park admission decreases, your Haunted House ticket must increase. I’ve discussed it with the other managers, and we believe fifty yuan is appropriate.”

“50?! Won’t that be too expensive?” Chen Ge had inherited the Haunted House from his parents, and he had not changed the pricing.

“If the quality justifies it, fifty is entirely reasonable. With park admission falling, people previously unwilling to pay the extra cost may visit. Prepare for large crowds over the next several days.” Director Luo sounded confident.

“Doubling the price might drive visitors away. There’s no end to the money one can chase, so why not proceed gradually?” Chen Ge regarded the Haunted House as his home. Life had only just returned to it, and losing visitors to a sudden price increase would genuinely sadden him.

“I’ve prepared a solution for that too.” Director Luo took back the document and turned to its final pages. Instead of blueprints, they contained a promotional plan for the park. “The futuristic park will soon launch a major campaign. We must move first and seize this opportunity with a large promotion of our own. Its central attractions will be the lower admission price and your Haunted House.”

“We’re tying the park with my Haunted House for the promotion?”

“At present, your Haunted House is New Century Park’s only real selling point.” The admission made Director Luo grimace. “If this campaign underperforms, it will probably be our last.”

The weight on Chen Ge’s shoulders abruptly increased. The entire park’s survival now depended upon him.

“Don’t feel too much pressure. To increase the attraction of the Haunted House and to make sure the visitors are willing to take the first step, I’ll be there to aid you.” This was also the last stand for Director Luo; they could not hold anything back.

“But none of you know how to design or operate a Haunted House.” This was Chen Ge’s territory, and it concealed too many secrets for outsiders to intervene.

“That may be true, but I know how to motivate visitors.” Director Luo clearly had a plan. “Uncle Xu tells me that when you divided the scenarios by difficulty, you offered a twenty-thousand-yuan prize?”

“That is true.” At the time, Chen Ge had been left with no other option. The separation was a safety net for the visitors as well. Pushing unprepared visitors into a three-star scenario directly might have led to some unforeseeable problems.

“It was an excellent idea, but twenty thousand is too little to attract widespread attention.” Director Luo pointed toward the open ground before the Haunted House. “Tomorrow, I’ll have a banner installed here announcing that the first person to clear every scenario will win two hundred thousand yuan in cash.”

“Two hundred thousand?” Chen Ge did not have even fifty thousand in his bank account. “Isn’t that excessive? What if someone actually succeeds?”

Director Luo stepped closer and lowered his voice, looking unlike his usual generous, kindly self. “That’s why I need you to design a challenge no one can clear. Let me be clear: if someone wins the two hundred thousand this week, I’ll pay only half. The rest comes from you.”

“So, you’re telling me to cheat?” Chen Ge felt troubled by the dishonesty.

“Why would you call it cheating? We are an amusement park; our purpose is to entertain visitors. When they learn that the first person to clear the Haunted House can win two hundred thousand yuan, will they be happy?” Director Luo patiently guided him through the logic.

“They definitely will. They get to visit the Haunted House and have a chance at winning the reward.”

“Then, when they find out that the cash prize has been taken by others, will they still be happy?”

“They will probably be disappointed.”

“Therefore, to keep every visitor happy, you must help me design a game no one can win.” Director Luo seemed satisfied with Chen Ge’s responses. “Xiao Chen, you’re a clever young man. Don’t disappoint me.”

Several years earlier, two hundred thousand yuan would have meant little to Director Luo, but circumstances had changed. Uncle Xu had told Chen Ge that to keep the park operating, Director Luo had mortgaged his own home a second time.

“Don’t worry, Director Luo. No one but me can clear this Haunted House. It is already an impossible game.”

“Then I’ll leave this to you. The promotion will officially start tomorrow.” Director Luo looked at the crowd outside of the Haunted House and walked away. He seemed several years younger.

That truly was good news. Whenever I help a lingering spirit or Specter resolve its regrets—or kill a monster from behind the door—my luck seems to improve.

Standing on the Haunted House steps, Chen Ge remembered experiencing something similar after destroying the mirror monster.
